AI Gateway concepts

An AI Gateway stores a reusable inference configuration. Pass the gateway’s ID or slug in the request’s model field, and AIVAX applies its model settings, instructions, RAG collections, tools, skills, workers, moderation, and context controls before calling the model.

Use a gateway when the same behavior must be reused by multiple clients or changed without redeploying the calling application. Use a direct inference call when the application controls the model, prompt, tools, and context of every request.

Treat the gateway configuration as sensitive: GET /api/v1/ai-gateways/<id> returns the full parameters to the owning account, including apiKey in plain text when the gateway uses an external provider key.

Responsibility boundary #

A gateway separates two roles:

  • The client application sends messages and, with a private key, optional request overrides.
  • The gateway administrator controls the operational policy: which model runs, what it is told, what it can read, which tools it can call, and which limits apply.

This boundary lets you change a model, a prompt, or a tool list in one place while every client keeps calling the same identifier. Each resource below is optional. Start with a model and system instructions, and add other resources only when the use case requires them: every tool, skill, or collection adds input tokens, cost, and one more path the model can choose wrongly.

The sections below describe what each resource does and when to use it. Processing pipeline documents the detailed behavior of each step.

Model and provider #

The gateway’s model is either an integrated AIVAX model or a model served by your own provider key (BYOK).

  • Integrated models use baseAddress: "@integrated" and a model name such as @openai/gpt-5-mini. AIVAX selects the provider, bills the account, and applies provider routing.
  • BYOK models use the base address of an OpenAI-compatible provider endpoint, your provider apiKey, and the provider’s model name. AIVAX still runs the gateway pipeline, but the provider bills you directly and provider routing does not apply. BYOK requests use the plan’s BYOK rate limit; see Plans and limits.

Use an integrated model unless you need a model, contract, or region that only your provider account offers. See Models and gateway names for how the model is identified.

Model routing #

Model routing selects a different model for each request. The complexity router classifies the latest user request as low, medium, or high complexity and runs the model configured for that level, with an optional reasoning effort per level. The response carries the X-Model-Routed-Complexity header when a level was selected.

Use it when most requests are simple but some need a stronger model, so you do not pay the stronger model’s price on every request. Do not use it when every answer must come from the same model for consistency or compliance.

Model routing differs from provider routing, which keeps the model and chooses which provider serves it.

Instructions #

Instruction settings shape the prompt the model receives:

ResourceWhat it doesWhen to use
System instructionsText added to the system instructions of every request.Always. Describe the role, audience, sources of truth, and limits.
Remote instruction sourcesURLs fetched as text and appended to the system instructions, with a configurable cache.Instructions maintained in another system, such as a CMS or a repository, that must change without editing the gateway.
User prompt templateReplaces {prompt} with the text of each user message.Every user message must be wrapped in the same frame, such as a fixed task description.
Assistant prefillInitial assistant text placed before generation.The answer must start with a fixed format. Some models do not support prefill.

Write instructions about behavior, not about settings the gateway already controls, such as truncation limits or the tool list. See Instructions for the remote source size limit and failure rules.

Model parameters #

The gateway can set default values for temperature, top_p, presence_penalty, frequency_penalty, stop, max_completion_tokens, reasoning_effort, verbosity, and seed. Requests sent with a private key can override most of them; see Override gateway values.

Set parameters on the gateway when the behavior must be the same for every client, for example a low temperature for an extraction assistant. Some integrated models reject parameters such as temperature, stop sequences, or reasoning effort; AIVAX rejects the gateway configuration when the limitation is known.

Context window and truncation #

contextMaximumSize limits the approximate number of input tokens sent to the model, and contextOverflowAction decides what happens when a conversation exceeds it:

  • Throw returns an error instead of calling the model. This is the default.
  • Truncate removes the oldest non-system messages until the conversation fits, then continues.
  • TruncateHard truncates like Truncate, but fails the request if the prompt still does not fit.

Use truncation for long-lived chats in which old turns lose relevance, such as support conversations. Keep Throw when every message matters, such as a document review, so the application decides what to remove. On the Free plan, the input context is capped regardless of this setting; see Limits.

Tool message truncation #

toolContextCount keeps only the most recent tool results intact. Older tool messages stay in the conversation, but their content is replaced with a short note asking the model to call the tool again.

Use it in long agentic conversations whose tools return large payloads that are only relevant once, such as search results. Avoid it when an early tool result remains important later. Rewriting old messages also changes the request prefix, which can reduce prompt caching.

Flags #

Flags change how AIVAX prepares the provider request for models with specific behavior. Configure them in Flags and normalization switches in the gateway editor or in parameters.flags.

FlagEffectWhen to use
DisableMultiModalInputImages, audio, video, and files are not sent to the model, even when it supports them.The gateway must stay text-only, for cost or policy reasons.
ThinkingProcessDeclares that the model reasons internally without returning its reasoning tokens.A model that reasons but hides its reasoning.
DiffusingStreamDeclares that the model is a diffusion model whose output is refined as a whole instead of produced token by token.Diffusion models only.
PreserveThinkingTokensKeeps the <think> blocks of earlier assistant messages in the conversation sent to the model.Models that need their previous reasoning to continue a multi-step task.
RewriteToolCallsAsUserMessagesRewrites tool calls and tool results as plain conversation messages.Models or providers that reject the native tool message format.
StrictUserAssistantTurnsEnforces strict alternation between user and assistant messages. This disables tool messages.Models that fail when two messages with the same role are adjacent.
DisableReasoningSummaryStops streaming reasoning content to the client.Clients that must never receive reasoning.

Flags compensate for model limitations. Leave them unset unless you observe the problem a flag solves.

Multimodal pre-processing #

Multimodal pre-processing converts images, audio, video, and files into text before the main model runs. Each media type uses its own engine: a smaller or larger multimodal model, OCR, or speech-to-text.

Use it when the main model is text-only, or when a cheaper model can describe media once and a stronger text model can reason about the description. Do not use it when the main model must see the original media, such as when comparing visual details. See Multimodal pre-processing for the engines and their billing.

Knowledge (RAG) #

A gateway can link collections so the model answers from your documents. The gateway controls the result limit, minimum score, reranker, reference behavior, and query strategy. Choose the strategy by conversation type:

  • Plain searches with the last user message. Use it for standalone questions.
  • Concatenate joins recent user messages. Use it when users split one question across several messages.
  • UserRewrite and FullRewrite rewrite recent messages into search queries with a resolver model. Use them when follow-up questions depend on earlier turns, at the cost of an extra inference.
  • QueryFunction gives the model a search tool so it decides when to search. Use it when many messages do not need retrieval. It requires a model with tool calling.

See RAG for the full behavior.

Tools #

Tools let the model act and read live data. A gateway can expose several kinds:

KindExecuted byWhen to use
Built-in toolsAIVAXCommon capabilities: date and time, web search, opening URLs, code, memory, and image, document, or page generation.
MCP sourcesYour MCP server, called by AIVAXYou already have an MCP server or a catalog of business tools shared by several agents.
Protocol functionsYour HTTP callback, called by AIVAXOne or a few specific actions, without running a full MCP server.
ShellAn AIVAX sandboxTasks easier to express as commands, or many tools moved behind a command line.
Raw toolsYour client applicationThe client must execute the action itself; see Tools.

Built-in tools, MCP tools, protocol functions, and the shell are server-side tools: AIVAX runs them during the request and returns only the final answer. Enable only tools with a clear role, and give them specific names and restrictive schemas.

Skills #

Skills are instruction packs the model loads on demand. Use them for specialized procedures that only some requests need, so their text does not occupy the system instructions of every request.

Tool handler #

The tool handler adds tool calling for models that do not produce reliable native tool calls. native or no value uses the model’s native tool calling; react.v1.selfcall uses a ReAct-style handler.

Use the handler only when a model you must use fails to call tools natively. Models with native tool calling are more reliable without it.

Tool explanations #

toolInvocationExplanations asks the model to explain each server-side tool call with a short reason and goal, which AIVAX returns with the tool event. Use it when the client shows tool activity to end users. See Tool explanations.

Moderation #

Input moderation evaluates the textual conversation before the main model runs and makes the model refuse requests that reach the configured sensitivity in a category. Use it for broad safety policy in user-facing assistants. It does not moderate output or media, and it is not an authorization mechanism. See Moderation.

Workers #

Workers call your endpoint during gateway events, so your code can block a message, rewrite context, add tools, or replace a tool result. Use them when a decision depends on data only your system has, such as the user’s account state. The worker runs in the critical path, so keep it fast and deterministic.

Time zone #

timeZone sets the IANA time zone the model uses to read and write dates. It applies to get_date_time, scheduling tools, and the shell, and defaults to America/Sao_Paulo. Set it to your users’ time zone; a request can override it with time_zone.

Pricing #

A gateway has no separate fee. Requests are billed by the model and the resources the gateway uses: inference tokens, rewrite or pre-processing inferences, moderation, tools, and RAG. See Inference pricing.
